label: Ubiquiti UniFi Switch 8 (Gen1)
description: Eight-port gigabit Layer 2 switch, no PoE, compact desktop enclosure.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Port Layout **8x 1 GbE RJ45 (1G/100M/10M)**, switching capacity 16 Gbps, non-blocking throughput 8 Gbps, forwarding rate 12 Mpps. **This is the plain US-8 - it has no PoE at all**; the US-8-60W in this catalogue has the same eight ports with four of them PoE. Same shape, same name stem, one letter different.

label: Ubiquiti UniFi Switch 8 (60W)
description: Eight-port gigabit Layer 2 switch with PoE on ports 5-8 and a 48 W total PoE budget.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Port Layout **8x 1 GbE RJ45, 4 with PoE**, **Max PoE output up to PoE (802.3af)**, **Total PoE availability 48 W**, switching capacity 16 Gbps. **Only four of the eight ports carry power, and the whole switch shares 48 W** - that is roughly two 802.3at-class loads or four 802.3af ones, so a PoE plan built on 'eight PoE ports' will overdraw it.

label: Ubiquiti USW Flex Mini
description: Five-port gigabit managed Layer 2 switch, powered by USB-C, no PoE output.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Port Layout **5x 1 GbE RJ45 (1G/100M/10M)**, switching capacity 10 Gbps, non-blocking throughput 5 Gbps, 1,000 VLANs. Managed, but **no PoE in either direction** - it is USB-C powered - so it cannot be the powered device on a PoE run, which is a common assumption for a five-port switch this size.

label: Ubiquiti USW Aggregation
description: Eight-port 10G SFP+ aggregation switch, rack mount 1U.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Port Layout **8x 10G SFP+ (10G/1G)**, switching capacity 160 Gbps, non-blocking throughput 80 Gbps, forwarding rate 119 Mpps. **All eight cages are SFP+ with no copper RJ45 ports at all** - there is no way to plug a copper link into this switch without a transceiver, and the 10G/1G note means a 1G optic works but a 2.5G or 5G SFP does not.

label: Ubiquiti USW Mission Critical
description: Nine-port gigabit Layer 3 switch with battery backup: four PoE+ ports, four PoE++ ports, 120 W PoE budget.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Port Layout **9x 1 GbE RJ45 (4 PoE+, 4 PoE++)**, **Total PoE availability 120 W**, **Redundancy: battery power backup**, Layer 3 supported, 18 Gbps switching capacity. Nine ports total means **eight powered and one unpowered**, and 120 W across four PoE++ ports is 30 W each at best - so a PoE++ device that wants more than that cannot be powered on this switch even before the PoE+ ports take their share.

label: Ubiquiti UniFi AC Long Range
description: Indoor 802.11ac access point with one gigabit port, long-range antenna design.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking Interface **(1) GbE RJ45 port**, channel bandwidth HT 20/40 and VHT 20/40/80 MHz. **A single gigabit port is the ceiling for the whole AP**: the two radios together exceed 1 Gbps of PHY rate, so any client load that maxes both bands is bounded by the copper, not the radio.

label: Ubiquiti UniFi U7 Pro Outdoor
description: Outdoor Wi-Fi 7 access point with one 1/2.5 GbE port, pole or wall mount.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking Interface **(1) 1/2.5 GbE RJ45 port**, wind loading 74.6 N at 200 km/h, pole mount 25-63.5 mm, UV-stabilised polycarbonate and aluminium. The **2.5G port is required** to make Wi-Fi 7 worthwhile - the same AP behind a gigabit port tops out at 1 Gbps of real traffic. Radio rates are modelled at Wi-Fi 7 class (688M on 2.4 GHz, 2.9G on 6 GHz) because the per-band rows were not in the extracted section.

label: Ubiquiti NanoSwitch
description: Outdoor four-port gigabit switch: one PoE-in port and three PoE passthrough ports, passive 24V.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking interface **(4) GbE RJ45 ports [(1) PoE-in, (3) PoE passthrough]**, total non-blocking line rate 4 Gbps, **Power method passive 24V 2-pair PoE-in**, supported voltage 21.6-30V, max power consumption **30 W**, POE-24-30W-G adapter **not included**. It is unmanaged: three ports repeat whatever PoE comes in, so the 30 W input is the budget for all three downstream devices combined.

label: Ubiquiti UFiber Loco
description: GPON ONT: one SC/APC GPON WAN port and one gigabit RJ45 LAN port, powered by micro-USB or 24V passive PoE.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking interface **(1) SC/APC ITU-G.984 GPON WAN port and (1) GbE RJ45 LAN port**, power method **micro-USB 5V 1A or 24V passive PoE (pins 4,5+ / 7,8-)**, micro-USB adapter included **only in the single-pack**. Two practical notes: the PoE-in is **passive 24V**, so an 802.3af switch port will not power it, and the multi-pack SKUs ship **without** the USB adapter.

label: Ubiquiti Wave MLO5
description: 60 GHz Wave AP with one 10G RJ45 port and one 10G SFP+ port, passive PoE.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking Interface **(1) 10 GbE RJ45 port and (1) 10G SFP+ port**, power method **passive PoE 4-pair or 2-pair, 44-54V DC (2-pair only above 44V)**, 54V 0.56A 10 GbE PoE adapter included, max power consumption 20 W. **Ten-gigabit on both ports** is unusual at this size and means the radio, not the copper, is the bottleneck; the 2-pair PoE mode requires at least 44V, so a 24V passive injector will not bring it up.

label: Ubiquiti UISP Switch Plus
description: Eight-port Layer 2 switch: four 1/2.5GbE RJ45 LAN ports and four 1/10G SFP+ cages, 50 Gbps non-blocking.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking interface **(4) 1/2.5 GbE RJ45 LAN ports and (4) 1/10G SFP+ ports**, total non-blocking throughput **50 Gbps**, switching capacity 100 Gbps, forwarding rate 74.4 Mpps, powered by an external AC/DC adapter or 27V DC Power TransPort input. **Half the ports are 2.5G copper and half are 10G fibre** - a plan that treats all eight as interchangeable will mis-place a 10G link on a 2.5G port.

label: Ubiquiti UACC Long-Range Endpoint
description: Long-range PoE endpoint for the LR Switch: two 100M ports, PoE+++ input with passthrough up to PoE++.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking interface **(2) 100M/10M ports**, power method **PoE+++**, max PoE output **passthrough up to PoE++**, max power consumption 2 W, supported voltage 52-57V, surge protection 3kA/6kV. **Both data ports are 100M** - this is an extender for long PoE runs, not a data-path switch, and putting it in front of a gigabit camera halves that camera's link.
